candidates.workingClaim: October 2, 1869: On October 2, 1869, Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born in Porbandar, India. A lawyer, politician, social activist, and writer, he became the leader of the Indian independence movement against British rule.
October 2, 1187: On October 2, 1187, Jerusalem surrendered to the army of Saladin after 88 years in the hands of the Franks. The capture followed his victory over a Crusader army at Hattin that July.
October 2, 1950: On October 2, 1950, the first Peanuts comic strip by Charles M. Schulz appeared in seven newspapers across the United States.
October 2, 1836: On October 2, 1836, HMS Beagle arrived back in England at Falmouth, ending a five-year voyage with the naturalist Charles Darwin aboard.

October 3, 1990: On October 3, 1990, the unification treaty between East and West Germany went into effect, making Germany a single state again. The treaty had been ratified by both German parliaments in September.
October 3, 1932: On October 3, 1932, Iraq was admitted to the League of Nations as an independent state.

October 3, 1789: On October 3, 1789, in New York, President George Washington issued a proclamation recommending Thursday, November 26, as a day of public thanksgiving for the people of the United States.
October 3, 1226: On October 3, 1226, Francis of Assisi, founder of the Franciscan religious orders, died in Assisi. He was canonized in 1228, and his feast day is October 4.
October 4, 1957: On October 4, 1957, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth.
October 4, 1966: On October 4, 1966, the Kingdom of Lesotho attained independence. The United States recognized it the same day and established an embassy at Maseru.
October 4, 1927: On October 4, 1927, carving began on Mount Rushmore in South Dakota. About 400 workers labored on the memorial until work ended on October 31, 1941.
October 4, 1669: On October 4, 1669, the Dutch Baroque painter and printmaker Rembrandt van Rijn died in Amsterdam. He is regarded as one of the greatest storytellers in the history of art.

October 5, 1962: On October 5, 1962, the Beatles released 'Love Me Do', backed by 'P.S. I Love You', as their first single. It reached number 17 in the United Kingdom and later became a US number one in 1964.
October 5, 1910: On October 5, 1910, Portugal's First Republic was declared from the balcony of Lisbon City Hall, the morning after a republican revolution began. King Manuel II escaped into exile.
October 5, 1908: On October 5, 1908, Ferdinand of Bulgaria proclaimed the full independence of Bulgaria from the Ottoman Empire and took the title of king, or tsar.
October 5, 1969: On October 5, 1969, the first episode of Monty Python's Flying Circus, 'Whither Canada?', aired, including the sketch 'The Funniest Joke in the World'.

October 6, 1995: On October 6, 1995, Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz of the University of Geneva announced at a conference in Florence the discovery of 51 Pegasi b, the first planet found orbiting a star other than the Sun. The discovery later earned them the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.
October 6, 1927: On October 6, 1927, The Jazz Singer, starring Al Jolson, was released. It was the first feature-length movie with synchronized dialogue.
October 6, 1973: On October 6, 1973, the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, Egypt and Syria attacked Israel simultaneously on two fronts, beginning the fourth of the Arab-Israeli wars.
October 6, 1981: On October 6, 1981, Anwar Sadat, president of Egypt since 1970, was assassinated in Cairo.

October 7, 1919: On October 7, 1919, Royal Dutch Airlines (KLM) was founded by eight investors from business and banking. It is the oldest airline in the world still operating under its original name.

October 7, 1571: On October 7, 1571, the fleets of the Holy League, including Spain, Venice, and the Papal States, defeated the Ottoman Turks in waters off southwestern Greece. Lepanto was the last great sea battle fought between galleys.

October 7, 1958: On October 7, 1958, NASA Administrator T. Keith Glennan approved the manned satellite project that became Project Mercury, America's first human spaceflight program, reportedly saying, in effect, 'Let's get on with it.'
October 7, 1949: On October 7, 1949, the German Democratic Republic, or East Germany, was founded when its provisional People's Chamber put the new state's constitution into force.

October 8, 1956: On October 8, 1956, New York Yankees pitcher Don Larsen threw a perfect game against the Brooklyn Dodgers, retiring all 27 batters. It remains the only perfect game in World Series history.
October 8, 1871: On October 8, 1871, a fire broke out in Chicago that burned until early October 10, devastating a wide swath of the city.
October 8, 1912: On October 8, 1912, Montenegro declared war on the Ottoman Empire, opening the First Balkan War. The other members of the Balkan League followed ten days later.

October 8, 1843: On October 8, 1843, Britain and China signed the Supplementary Treaty of the Bogue (Humen). It gave British citizens extraterritoriality, the right to be tried by British courts, and most-favored-nation status in China.
